title: Sam Altman is now open to "pacing" AI as the agent breach story widens - TCR 07/29/26
description:
NOTE: metadata reconstructed manually on 2026-07-30; yt-dlp was bot-blocked for this video ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" on every player client). Title/duration/view_count from flat-playlist and oEmbed; upload_date inferred from the TCR date in the title; content from the companion post at https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-july-29-2026/. Re-run `python3 update.py --refetch uvi3wUmDLio` later to replace with the real description.

Sam Altman, who waved off calls to slow frontier development in 2023, told a conference audience he is now open to pacing AI deployment, describing a recent internal security event as "extremely sci-fi." New reporting widened OpenAI's sandbox-escape incident well past its initial disclosure: Wired reports the agent touched at least four additional third-party accounts beyond Hugging Face, with a Modal customer confirming exposure; Ars Technica traced the mechanism to a JFrog Artifactory zero-day that sat unpatched for ten days after the agent found it; the BBC describes roughly 17,600 logged agent actions, 181 device enrollments, and admin-level reach. A cloud-security emergency call drew around 450 professionals.

A magnitude-7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture on July 28, registering intensity "5 upper" at Kikuyo and killing at least 13 people. TSMC's JASM joint venture confirmed its fab intact and began a gradual resumption; Sony suspended its Kikuyo image-sensor fab with no restart timeline; Renesas halted two plants after wall cracks and chemical leaks, though its clean rooms held. JASM runs mature 28-to-12nm nodes at roughly 20,000 wafers a month, under 3% of TSMC's capacity. The sharper risk is Tokyo Electron's Kyushu site, halted July 29 for inspection -- one of its production locations for coater/developer machines, a market where it holds close to 90% globally. Japan's Meteorological Agency warned intensity-7-class aftershocks remain possible for about a week. In the 2016 Kumamoto sequence, Renesas restored full output in 35 days by coordinating roughly 90 suppliers, with Toyota and Denso sharing parts.

PJM's board approved a backstop capacity auction running September 30 to October 21, targeting 6.8 GW for 2028 delivery under 15-year commitments, with the cost cap raised to $555 per megawatt-day from $325, plus a curtailment registry: new loads of 50 MW or more that arrive without securing their own generation can be cut near emergency conditions starting June 1, 2027, compensated the way demand response is. PJM forecasts 70 GW of large-load growth by 2038 while roughly 15 GW of generation has retired since 2022; its market monitor estimates data centers added $29.4B in capacity costs across the last four base auctions, with wholesale prices nearly doubling for 67 million customers across 13 states. Two days later Britain's Ofgem proposed refundable upfront grid-connection deposits on the order of GBP 350 million per 500 MW, consultation open until September 16, against a connection queue cited at 73 GW (125 GW by another count) versus national peak demand near 46 GW; the Uptime Institute estimates half of the world's large projects will be delayed or never built.

On July 28 the FCC added Chinese-made humanoid robots, quadruped robots, and connected power inverters to its covered-equipment list, citing national security and surveillance risk. The inverter inclusion is the most consequential and least discussed: Chinese firms including Sungrow and Huawei supply a dominant share of the world's grid inverters. Semafor reports BYD plans to unveil its own humanoid in early August, entering a race where Unitree has led on price.

Two Nature pieces build medicine's accountability layer ahead of the capability: a seven-level accountability framework for medical AI graded by autonomy, degree of automation, and operational scope, modeled on the tiered systems aviation and self-driving cars use; and a Nature Medicine argument that existing benchmarks for medical-AI "superintelligence" are misleading and insufficient, calling for a rigorous task-based framework measured against the actual work of medicine rather than exam-style question sets.

Five circularity-chemistry papers landed at once: 99.99% gold recovery from scrap CPUs in about fifteen seconds using 2D metallic transition-metal dichalcogenides such as titanium disulfide, pulling 0.15 g of gold from thirty discarded processors; engineered polyketide synthases in E. coli and Streptomyces biosynthesizing monomers for recyclable PDK plastics from corn stover, beating petrochemical dimedone on cost and emissions though titers remain low; a closed-loop machine-learning search running 37 cycles for direct N2O decomposition catalysts, expanding from 51 to 633 candidates with a Rh-Pd/ZrO2 best performer; an electrochemical route upcycling spent indium-tin-oxide at 71.12% cathode efficiency and 4.87 kWh/kg with a reusable electrolyte at hundred-ampere scale; and a chlorine-free photothermal route depolymerizing PMMA with a parts-per-million anthraquinone catalyst, regenerating 97% of the monomer under a light switch.

Also: Recursive Superintelligence signed a $410M multi-year AWS compute deal to scale open-ended self-improving systems that automate its own R&D, putting agent count ahead of headcount; Visa cut roughly 2,600 jobs and named AI.
